notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0012] Mirror sibling module patterns for errors, money, and audit: Before writing a new function, read adjacent modules (payments.py, money.py, errors.py, audit.py) and reuse their helpers and error codes for consistency.
  Use `round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, and `BillingError(code, detail)` with codes like `invalid_state`, `non_positive_amount`. Validate state (e.g. status must be 'captured'), reject non-positive amounts, and cap cumulative refunds at the captured amount before mutating `refunded_amount`/`status`.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and zero: When implementing monetary functions, import and use the repo's existing round_money and ZERO constants rather than ad-hoc round() calls.
  Inspect sibling modules (e.g. payments.py) to find shared helpers like round_money and ZERO, then apply them consistently so rounding and comparisons match the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0007] Reuse existing period arithmetic helpers: When implementing a new time-based function, look for an existing sibling function doing similar period math and mirror its structure.
  Before writing renewal/period logic, grep for related functions (e.g. current_period) and reuse their exact pattern: normalize inputs with ensure_utc, compute length = timedelta(days=period_days), and use floor division (at - start) // length. This keeps semantics consistent and avoids off-by-one bugs.
- [rb-0009] Normalize datetimes via the project's ensure_utc: Use the repository's existing ensure_utc helper rather than ad-hoc tzinfo checks so naive/invalid inputs raise the project's BillingError.
  Inspect clock.py/errors.py early; calling ensure_utc on both the query time and stored timestamps gives consistent UTC comparison and correct error codes for naive datetimes, matching hidden-test expectations.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.
- [rb-0002] Inspect existing module conventions before implementing: Reading sibling functions in the target file reveals required helpers and patterns like to_money, ZERO, and round_money.
  Before writing a new function, read the surrounding module (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to see how money is normalized and rounded. Mirror those conventions so the new function is consistent and passes hidden tests.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

item.title: Check for repo-wide conventions before implementing a new operation
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it missed a team convention (idempotency_key) that applied to all money-moving operations, not just the one being added.
item.content: Before writing a new payment/credit/invoice operation, grep the repo for existing conventions like idempotency_key, audit event patterns, and keyword-only params, and check for docs/CHANGELOG notes about incidents. Apply cross-cutting conventions even when the issue text doesn't mention them.

item.title: Implement idempotency by checking audit events first
item.description: Idempotent operations must look up prior audit entries by key before validating state or mutating anything.
item.content: Add `*, idempotency_key=None` to the signature, then first scan audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the original result if found. Only after that do state validation and mutation, and include idempotency_key in the audit.record call.

item.title: Mirror sibling functions for state transitions and audit
item.description: Following the existing authorize/invoice patterns (BillingError invalid_state, ensure_utc, audit.record naming) produced a consistent implementation.
item.content: When adding a state-transition function, copy the structure of an existing sibling: raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...) with the current status, normalize times with ensure_utc, and record an audit event named <entity>_<action> with the relevant fields.
